the presence of antinucleic acid antibodies in patients with SLE and RA does not appear to be a consequence of a viral infection, and that the presence of such antibodies is not a useful marker of a preceding viral illness.
antipolynuclotide antibodies are seen in patients with SLE, RA and JRA, and are not seen in the sera of normal individuals.

the prevalence of antineuclotide antibodies in the serum of patients with connectivit tissue diseases is high.

antinuclear antibody (ANA) testing is not a good test to screen for SLE, but rather a poor screening test.
